title: Generalisation attempts in the twin-prime-parity programme: character weights, the shift-2 core, and angle parity
summary: Three generalisation attempts with their verdicts; no twin primes or Chowla conjecture are proved. A q-periodic coefficient makes the boundary functional a character-weighted geometric sum: the regrouping, the forced leading equation x^s=1-x^q with roots 1/sqrt2 and (sqrt5-1)/2, and its failure for chi_3 and chi_4 are proved in Lean. Only 1349 of 4537 (chi,r) pairs over real characters mod q<=60 admit a threshold. The shift-2 split reduces the open core to a sum of lambda over a quadratic polynomial, and the spectral input does not break parity over Q, though it does over F_q[T]. Angle twists are pair-invisible up to O(t log N).
